Running a frontline business is an operational puzzle most software has never touched. Shift-by-shift labour costs, compliance that changes by region and by role, and margins thin enough that a badly built rota can sink a quarter. It's a harder problem than most white-collar SaaS, and yet frontline sectors employ 80% of the global workforce and have received about 1% of the last decade's software investment.

We think that's because the problem needed AI, not just better software, before it was solvable. Frontline organisations sit on enormous amounts of operational data. Used properly, that data lets agents take on real parts of running the business rather than just reporting on it. That's what we're building at Sona, and it's early enough that the systems you build now will still be foundational in three years.

We've raised over $100M from N47, Felicis, Gradient and Northzone, signed more than 100 enterprise customers across the UK and US, and opened offices in London, New York, Austin and Lisbon. More on working at Sona here.

About the Role

We're hiring Senior Software Engineers to join our product teams and help build the next generation of workforce management. This isn't a traditional engineering role - at Sona, engineers are deeply embedded in the product development process, working directly with customers to understand their pain points and turning those insights into shipped solutions.

AI tooling is central to how we work. Coding agents produce the majority of our code, and your job is to direct, correct, and architect - not type every line yourself. You'll use tools like Claude Code, Cursor, or similar as a core part of your daily workflow, and we'll assess that proficiency as part of the interview process. To do that well, you need strong Elixir expertise - enough to know when an agent's output is wrong and how to fix it.

Day to day, you'll work within a cross-functional product team with significant autonomy over how to reach outcomes. You'll participate in defining features and scope from PR FAQs and kick-off conversations rather than picking up fully specified tickets. You'll also have the opportunity to rotate across different product domains throughout the year - scheduling, payroll, HR, staff engagement - giving you breadth that most engineering roles don't offer.

This role is remote-first for anyone based in a European timezone, with quarterly in-person team alignment sessions and client workshops in London. It's not a fully isolated remote setup - you'll need flexibility to travel for the moments that matter.

Responsibilities

  • Own features end-to-end across Sona's platform, from scoping through to delivery, including in the mobile app

  • Use AI development tooling as your primary workflow - directing and evaluating agent-produced code, not writing everything from scratch

  • Work directly with customers through workshops, feedback sessions, and discovery conversations to ensure what you build solves real problems

  • Collaborate closely with Product Managers and Product Designers to shape solutions from vague requirements and kick-off outputs

  • Contribute to multiple product domains across the year, building deep understanding of workforce management challenges

  • Participate in the product development process - challenging scope, suggesting approaches, and making pragmatic trade-offs between the ideal solution and the right one for now

Requirements

  • You're a senior engineer who's comfortable owning features from scoping to production - not just executing against a spec

  • You have professional Elixir experience - enough to evaluate and correct agent-produced code in a production codebase

  • AI development tooling is already embedded in how you work, not something you've experimented with once or twice. You can articulate your workflows and demonstrate them under pressure

  • You care about understanding customer problems as much as solving technical ones, and you're comfortable being in front of customers directly

  • You communicate clearly and concisely - adapting for technical and non-technical audiences alike

  • You're pragmatic: you can let go of a strongly held opinion when the situation calls for it, and you make trade-offs consciously

  • Bonus: full-stack experience including React Native, background at a product-led engineering team or high-growth B2B SaaS company, or familiarity with HR/workforce management domains

Benefits

  • Salary: £85-105k

  • Remote-first (Europe timezone) with quarterly in-person sessions and client workshops in London

  • Share options

  • 35 days annual leave (25 days standard plus 10 flexible public holiday days)

  • Extra day of leave for every year of service

  • Pension contributions matched up to 5%

  • Comprehensive health insurance

  • Enhanced parental leave & pay

  • Salary sacrifice childcare scheme (Workplace Nursery)

  • Co-working space stipend for those based outside London

  • Annual all expenses paid team retreats

  • The latest Macbook and equipment budget for your home office

  • Professional development budget

  • Unlimited free books

Note: this represents a typical salary and benefits package for a UK-based, full-time employee. Contexte de la mission

Orion est une plateforme SaaS interne permettant aux équipes marketing de configurer, lancer et gérer des services sur différents marchés et lignes de services, sans support technique.

Votre rôle portera sur le cœur de la plateforme et sa couche d’intégration : système de modules, connecteurs et API permettant de transformer le lancement d’un service sur plusieurs marchés en un exercice de configuration plutôt qu’en un projet de six mois.

L’environnement comprend notamment :

  • Des modules de services pluggables.
  • Des Web Components intégrables.
  • Des parcours de configuration pilotés par des machines à états.
  • Des intégrations avec un écosystème composé de CMS, plateformes e-commerce, CRM et plateformes data.


Il s’agit d’un rôle orienté plateforme, dont les utilisateurs sont d’autres ingénieurs, les équipes métier et les services eux-mêmes. Le succès se mesure notamment à la capacité à intégrer de nouveaux services beaucoup plus rapidement que lors des premiers déploiements, avec l’ambition de générer une amélioration de 10x plutôt que de 10 %.

ResponsabilitésConstruire le cœur de la plateforme

  • Concevoir et implémenter les primitives de la plateforme.
  • Développer le modèle de contenu à plusieurs niveaux : templates → masters → instances.
  • Mettre en place l’édition basée sur les rôles.
  • Concevoir les workflows de revue et de publication.
  • Développer des parcours UX pilotés par des machines à états afin de simplifier les configurations complexes.


Piloter la couche d’intégration

  • Construire les connecteurs et API permettant aux nouveaux services de se connecter à Orion.
  • Intégrer Orion à l’écosystème technologique global.


Concevoir une architecture modulaire

  • Faire évoluer le monorepo composé du cœur de la plateforme et de modules de services pluggables.
  • Permettre l’ajout de nouvelles catégories de services via des patterns réutilisables plutôt que par une réécriture complète.
  • Concevoir des solutions capitalisant sur les développements existants.


Développer des expériences intégrables

  • Concevoir et faire évoluer la couche Web Components permettant de déployer les services configurés dans Orion sur des sites web et plateformes externes.


Faire évoluer l’architecture

  • Contribuer aux décisions d’architecture et les challenger via le processus de RFC.
  • Formaliser et documenter les choix techniques.


Garantir la qualité

  • Maintenir des standards élevés de qualité de code, de tests et de documentation.
  • Garantir la stabilité de la plateforme et limiter les régressions.


Compétences techniques indispensablesReact

Maîtrise avancée de la conception d’interfaces complexes et performantes, notamment :

  • Machines à états pour les parcours UX, XState ou équivalent.
  • Patterns de conception de composants et design systems, notamment Tailwind et ShadCN.
  • Web Components, architectures intégrables et micro-frontends.
  • Optimisation des performances.
  • Frameworks de test : Jest, React Testing Library, Playwright.


JavaScript, TypeScript et Node.js

  • Solide expertise en développement Full Stack moderne.
  • Conception et versioning d’API consommées par d’autres équipes : REST/OpenAPI et GraphQL.
  • Maîtrise des patterns asynchrones et event-driven.
  • Authentification et autorisation à grande échelle : JWT, OAuth, RBAC.


Architecture logicielle

  • Conception de systèmes sur lesquels d’autres équipes peuvent construire.
  • Architecture hexagonale, ports et adaptateurs, ou approche comparable de séparation des responsabilités.
  • Monorepo modulaire et gestion des dépendances.
  • Points d’extension, systèmes de plugins ou SDK permettant à d’autres développeurs de s’appuyer sur les abstractions existantes.


Architecture serverless sur GCP

Expérience pratique du développement et du déploiement d’applications serverless sur Google Cloud Platform, notamment :

  • Cloud Run et Cloud Functions.
  • API Gateway.
  • Cloud Storage.
  • Cloud SQL PostgreSQL.
  • Cloud Firestore.


Compétences fortement souhaitées

  • Maturité dans la conception d’API : versioning, rétrocompatibilité, dépréciation et évolution sans rupture pour les systèmes consommateurs.
  • Multi-tenancy : isolation, configuration et montée en charge pour plusieurs marchés ou clients.
  • Design systems : design tokens et pipelines automatisés de Figma jusqu’à la production.
  • Développement agentique ou assisté par IA, avec une approche coding-first.

  • CI/CD et Infrastructure as Code : pipelines CI/CD et Terraform pour les tests automatisés, le déploiement et la gestion de l’infrastructure.
  • Sécurité applicative : principes de sécurité des applications web et pratiques de secure coding.

  • Expérience en optimisation des performances front-end à grande échelle.

Notre processus de recrutement :

Conçu pour être rapide et transparent. Voici les étapes :

1- Contact téléphonique : Si votre CV est retenu, nous vous contacterons pour un échange téléphonique

2- Entretien RH : Un rendez-vous d'une heure avec un membre de l’équipe RH pour discuter de votre parcours, de vos compétences et vous présenter SII et ce que nous pouvons vous apporter tout au long de votre carrière.

3- Entretien avec un Business Manager : Une rencontre avec un de nos business managers pour un échange sur l’environnement de travail, le contexte et les missions du ou des postes associés.

4- Rencontre avec notre client : La dernière étape du processus est un rendez-vous avec notre client dans leurs locaux ou en visioconférence.

5- Retour / Décision final sur votre recrutement : Suite aux échanges précédents, nous vous indiquerons si le dernier entretien a été concluant : si c’est le cas, nous vous effectuerons une proposition de collaboration orale, qui vous sera transmise par mail, afin de pouvoir avancer ensemble vers un recrutement.

Si l’échange ne correspondait pas aux attentes du client / chef de projet : nous vous indiquerons les raisons de la fin du process de recrutement.

About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

Edge Functions are server-side TypeScript functions, distributed globally at the edge - close to your users. They power use cases such as webhook receivers, AI inferences, OG image generation and real-time bots (Slack, Discord, etc). Built on top of Supabase Edge Runtime: an open-source, Deno-based runtime written in Rust that runs JavaScript, TypeScript, and WASM services.

We want developers to be able to build truly global applications by distributing both compute and data globally. Infrastructure concerns like regions, cold starts, CPU and memory provisioning should fade into the background so developers can focus on iterating on business logic.

We are looking for experienced and passionate engineers to help us go further in this vision.

What You’ll Own

  • Evolving Supabase Edge Runtime - an Open-sourced Rust-based host that runs the Deno isolate, manages the main/user runtime split, and enforces per-request memory and CPU limits.

  • Implementing monitoring, alerting, and OpenTelemetry tracing across the runtime, then using that visibility to drive optimizations that improve latency and reliability of the service.

  • Working closely with the Deno and other open-source teams, contributing to upstream and relaying our users' requirements.

  • Participating in an on-call rotation to keep Edge Functions healthy in production.

  • Help manage and improve features like scheduled functions, background tasks, WebSockets streaming, ephemeral file storage, and custom routing.

  • Integrating functions more tightly with the rest of the Supabase stack - Auth, Postgres, Storage, and Realtime.

  • Expanding functions to support more use cases (AI inference, MCP servers, hosting simple websites, URL shorteners).

  • Improving the DX of developing and debugging functions locally through the Supabase CLI, including DevTools integration, logging, and production parity.

What You’ll Bring

  • At least 5 years of backend or systems engineering experience, with strong fluency in Rust and TypeScript.

  • Experience with V8 Isolates, Deno and the JavaScript runtimes in general.

  • Experience operating infrastructure at scale - Kubernetes, AWS, Cloudflare Workers, Redis, or comparable systems.

  • A strong vision for how compute and data can be pushed to the edge.

  • Bonus: experience building developer-facing CLIs or front-end tooling that sits on top of an infrastructure product.

What We Offer

  • Fully Remote

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

  • ESOP

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

  • Tech Allowance

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

  • Health Benefits

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

  • Annual Off-Sites

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

  • Flexible Work

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

  • Professional Development

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

  • ~400 team members

  • 60+ countries

  • 20+ languages spoken

  • Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

  • 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

The grid was built for predictable, centralised power. Today it's absorbing intermittent supply from grid scale solar and wind, alongside dynamic demand from EVs, heat pumps, and home batteries. The missing piece is software that can connect and orchestrate these devices at scale.

Enode provides the infrastructure layer that makes this possible. Our Connect API gives energy companies a single integration to 1000+ devices across 80+ brands. Our optimisation tooling gives energy companies the building blocks to manage those devices locally - think smart charging for EVs. Our Flex product turns those connected devices into a flexible, controllable asset for energy companies.

We work with device manufacturers across the energy hardware ecosystem - from EV brands to heat pump and solar inverter producers. Our customers are energy retailers, utilities, and traders building the next generation of energy services. We're backed by Y Combinator, Lowercarbon Capital, and Creandum.

You'll build integrations with leading OEMs and help mature our API surface into the unified control layer for the home, at a moment when customer demand for battery and home energy optimization is accelerating.

  • Work with partnership and commercial teams on API feasibility for new OEM integrations.

On recrute peu, et jamais par réflexe : ce poste n’est pas un renfort d’urgence sur une équipe débordée, c’est un choix, on a la conviction qu’un développeur de plus change ce qu’on est capable de construire, pas juste la vitesse à laquelle on livre l’existant.

Concrètement, ça veut dire des sujets produit prêts qui attendent une capacité de dev supplémentaire, et des sujets techniques qu’on veut enfin traiter avec le sérieux qu’ils méritent plutôt que de les faire glisser d’un trimestre à l’autre : monitoring, qualité, enrichissement de données, commerce agentique. On ne recrute pas quelqu’un pour tenir une file de tickets. On recrute pour élargir ce qu’on est capable de construire.

Le poste en une phrase

Livrer du produit de bout en bout sur l’ensemble de nos projets back, puis prendre la responsabilité d’un des sujets transverses (données, monitoring, infra, IA appliquée) parce qu’il t’intéresse, pas parce que personne d’autre ne le fait.

Un périmètre back qui ne se limite pas à l’API

Notre back n’est pas un monolithe unique. Tu interviendras sur :

  • notre API principale en Ruby on Rails;

  • nos projets internes et services intermédiaires en TypeScript / NestJS, qui contiennent entre autres, un serveur MCP, des agents customs, une librairie partagée pour les règles métiers.

  • les outils internes qui font tourner l’équipe : CI, monitoring, scripts de données.

Savoir livrer propre est un prérequis, pas la mission. La mission, c’est de faire avancer un sujet quel que soit le projet dans lequel il atterrit.

Notre manière de travailler avec l’IA générative

On l’utilise au quotidien (Cursor) mais l’outil n’est pas le sujet. Ce qui compte, c’est ce qu’on a construit autour : des skills et des process partagés qui cadrent son usage et une règle non négociable, l’auteur d’une PR répond de chaque ligne, quelle que soit la façon dont elle a été écrite.

Concrètement, ça change deux choses pour toi :

  • Le coût d’entrée dans un projet que tu ne connais pas baisse fortement. C’est ce qui nous permet de te proposer un périmètre large sans te demander de maîtriser toutes nos stacks au départ, tu resteras responsable de comprendre ce que tu livres, mais tu ne partiras pas de zéro.

  • La question de la connaissance est un sujet de travail en soi chez nous : comment une équipe continue à comprendre son propre code quand une partie est écrite avec assistance. On n’a pas fini d’y répondre, et tu contribueras à cette réflexion.

Ce que tu feras dès les premières semaines

  • Prendre des sujets produit de A à Z : cadrage technique avec le produit, conception, implémentation, tests, mise en prod, suivi.

  • Développer et faire évoluer nos services back, sur Rails comme sur NestJS.

  • Tenir la qualité, tests, revues de code, arbitrages de dette, non comme une case à cocher, mais comme la condition pour que l’équipe garde de la vitesse.

  • Challenger l’existant et les besoins mal définis. On préfère quelqu’un qui relance et recadre plutôt que quelqu’un qui attend une spec parfaite.

Sur les 6 premiers mois, selon tes envies

Ces sujets sont ouverts, pas attribués. On n’attend pas que tu arrives compétent sur les cinq, on attend que tu en prennes un et que tu le fasses avancer pour de vrai.

  • Enrichissement de nos données produits et recettes.

  • Améliorations des fonctionnalité agentiques, exploration des workflows et des sous-agents pour faire ses courses plus facilement.

  • Structuration d’outils pour les rendre disponibles sur chaque providers IAs et sur nos propres agents grâce à nos MCPs.

  • Notre infra as code (Terraform).

  • Constructions de nouveaux algorithmes de personnalisation, exploitation de nos statistiques dans les features.

Ce que ce poste n’est pas

  • Pas un poste de spécialiste data ou ML : si tu veux modéliser à plein temps, tu t’ennuieras.

  • Pas un poste d’exécution de tickets : tu auras le contexte produit, un mot à dire sur l’architecture, et la responsabilité de ce que tu mets en prod.

  • Pas un poste d’architecte détaché du code : on conçoit et on implémente dans la même semaine.

Notre stack

  • Ruby on Rails

  • NestJS / TypeScript

  • un peu de Python

  • GCP, Terraform

Pourquoi nous rejoindre

  • Une équipe à taille humaine où les décisions techniques se prennent en équipe.

  • Un produit à fort impact et de vraies contraintes d’échelle.

  • Des temps d’équipe réguliers : afterworks, déjeuners, teambuildings, séminaire annuel.

Modalités

  • CDI, rémunération de 38k à 46k annuel selon profil.

  • Bureaux à Euratechnologies, à 10 min du centre de Lille en métro.

  • Télétravail jusqu’à 50% du temps.

  • Mutuelle Alan, titres restaurant Swile, prise en charge à 50 % de l’abonnement transports en commun et de l’abonnement V’Lille.

Deux prérequis :

  • Bac +5 en informatique ou équivalent (école d’ingénieur, master). On tient à un socle scientifique solide : maths, stats, raisonnement logique, parce que les sujets sur lesquels tu évolueras en ont besoin.

  • Solide sur Ruby / Rails ou sur TypeScript / NestJS. Pas les deux. Si tu ne maîtrises que l’un, tu apprendras l’autre chez nous, et c’est explicitement ce qu’on attend de toi.

Au-delà de ça :

  • Tu as au moins 2 ans d’expérience et tu livres proprement.

  • Tu es autonome sur un sujet de A à Z. Quand tu es bloqué, tu changes d’angle ou tu viens en parler, tu ne restes pas bloqué trois jours.

  • Tu réfléchis aux conséquences de ce que tu construis : produit, technique, architecture, maintenance.

  • Tu es pragmatique : la solution simple et adaptée au contexte plutôt que la solution impressionnante.

  • Tu utilises l’IA générative dans ton travail et tu sais où sont ses limites. Tu assumes le code que tu produis, y compris celui que tu n’as pas tapé toi-même, et l’idée de travailler dans un cadre partagé plutôt qu’en improvisation t’intéresse.

  • Tu as un intérêt réel pour au moins un de nos sujets transverses : data, infra, monitoring, qualité logicielle, IA appliquée.

  • Ça ne te bloque pas de passer une journée sur le front, la CI ou des logs quand le sujet l’exige.

  • Tu partages : review, entraide, documentation, communication.

Ce qu’on ne te demande pas :

  • D’être expert en data, en infra ou en front.

  • D’avoir déjà fait exactement ce poste ailleurs.

  • De connaître toutes nos stacks.

  1. Premier échange en visio (30 min): avec Sacha, lead Backend : ton parcours, ce que tu cherches, et de notre côté une présentation plus précise de ce qu’on peut te demander pour vérifier le fit.

  2. Entretien technique dans nos locaux (~2h) : Vraie mise en situation sur un de nos sujets : on te l’expose et on te demande d’expliquer comment tu le résoudrais de A à Z. On veut surtout évaluer ta capacité de réflexion, tes réflexes et l’usage d’outils d’IA générative.

  3. On s’engage à te donner une réponse sous deux semaines.

Unser Data & Automation Team unterstützt andere Abteilungen des OMR Kosmos, u.a. auch das Sales & Partnerships Team bei der Betreuung der spannendsten nationalen und internationalen Partner*innen aus dem Digital- und Brandbereich. Zum Produktportfolio gehören neben unserem OMR Festival auch zahlreiche Podcast Formate, eine Jobbörse, die Software Bewertungsplattform OMR Reviews sowie unsere umfangreichen OMR Education Produkte, u.v.m. 

Du bist analytisch sehr versiert, liebst es, Zahlen, Daten und Fakten zu konsolidieren und zu analysieren? Du hast Spaß daran, strategische Schlussfolgerungen aus Daten zu ziehen, die wirklich etwas bewegen? Dann freuen wir uns auf dich!


Wo du wirklich was bewegst


  • Du hast ein Auge für Prozesse und hast Lust, bestehende Arbeitsabläufe zu automatisieren und Erkenntnisse aus Daten zu gewinnen
  • Du unterstützt bei der Erstellung und Aufbereitung sowie der Weiterentwicklung der Sales & Partnerships Strategie und der Jahresplanung
  • Du analysierst und bereitest die strategischen Ziele unserer Partner auf und identifizierst Potenziale im OMR Kosmos
  • Du analysierst diverse Datenquellen (u.a. CRM-Daten, Statista, etc.) und erstellst Prozesse inklusive Auswertungen und Analysen zur Verbesserung unserer Sales-Aktivitäten
  • Du recherchierst potenziell neue Branchen, Industriesektoren und Ansprechpartner*innen
  • Du steigerst die Datenqualität, verknüpfst die Daten innerhalb des OMR Kosmos und bereitest diese in Dashboard- und Präsentationsform auf
  • Du recherchierst und bewertest das bestehende Tool Stack bei OMR und die besten Tools auf dem Markt
  • Du arbeitest eng mit unserem Sales & Partnerships Team sowie abteilungsübergreifend mit vielen weiteren Teams aus dem OMR Kosmos zusammen
  • Du arbeitest nicht nur ab, sondern bringst dich und deine Ideen aktiv mit ein


Was dich auszeichnet


  • Du bist eingeschriebene*r Student*in an einer deutschen Hochschule -  im Bereich IT, Wirtschaft, VWL, Finance oder einem vergleichbaren Studiengang
  • Du nutzt die für deinen Job zentralen Programme wie Google Workspace und CRM-Systeme und bringst ein starkes Interesse und Verständnis für Automation- und Script-Tools mit (z. B. make.com, zapier, n8n)
  • Du hast erste Kenntnisse in SQL oder Programmiersprachen wie Python oder TypeScript
  • Idealerweise hast du bereits mit den Tools der Google Suite gearbeitet
  • Du denkst analytisch und hast ein gutes Auge für Zahlen, Daten und Fakten
  • Du arbeitest strukturiert, zielorientiert und selbstständig


Was für dich drin ist


  • Die Möglichkeit, dich in einem der spannendsten deutschen Medienunternehmen einzubringen
  • Ein Wohlfühl-Office mit höhenverstellbaren Tischen, Massage-Sesseln, Mini-Gym, Sommer-Deck uvm. direkt im Hamburger Schanzenviertel
  • Von unserem Campus-Team frisch zubereitete Leckereien sowie großes Müsli- und Getränkeangebot 
  • Firmenfitness über EGYM Wellpass und Mental-Health-Angebote von nilo 
  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten und heycare für die Betreuung von Kids, Vierbeiner oder die Pflege von Angehörigen und mehr Vereinbarkeit im Alltag
  • Zuschuss zur HVV-Proficard und Mitarbeiterrabatte auf Partnerprodukte
  • Zugang zu allen OMR-Weiterbildungsformaten und eine steile Lernkurve in digitalen Themenfeldern
  • Die Gelegenheit, dich über den OMR Kosmos mit den Player*innen der Digitalszene zu vernetzen

We're looking for a Product Engineer (m/f/d) to join our Tech team at Buying Labs ideally based in Hamburg or remotely for the right fit. In this role, you'll combine deep technical skill with strong product thinking to build tools and features using AI that create real value for our users and our business. You'll own features end to end - from scoping and design through development, deployment, and adoption - and use AI to build smarter and faster at every step.

This is a role for builders who care about impact: people who understand both the user perspective and the underlying business processes, who can scope what needs to be built and then make it happen.


Your Mission

  • End-to-End Product Delivery: Own features from concept to production and real users, not just code -ship complete solutions that drive measurable business value. Scope requirements, define technical approaches, and deliver across frontend and backend, with quality built in from the start and verified through appropriate testing.
  • Product Thinking & User Focus: Understand user needs and business processes to identify what should be built and why. Translate product ideas and stakeholder input into shipped experiences that users actually adopt.
  • Building AI into Products: Design and integrate AI-powered features into our platform - not just using coding assistants, but building AI solutions that solve real problems for our users. Identify opportunities where AI can speed up workflows, improve decision-making, or unlock new capabilities.
  • Data Modelling & Scalable Systems: Build solid data models and scalable architectures that serve as a reliable foundation for our products. Turn repeated work into shared building blocks (UI components, data import flows, AI pipelines) so each new tool is faster to build than the last.
  • Stakeholder Collaboration & Adoption: Work with stakeholders at all levels - from leadership to operations - to align on priorities and drive adoption of new tools and features. Communicate technical concepts clearly and build buy-in for your solutions across the organisation.
  • Continuous Improvement: Gather feedback early, iterate quickly, and continuously improve what you build. Stay current with emerging technologies and engineering best practices to keep our tools & systems ahead of what the business needs to keep the platform competitive.

  • Experience integrating ERPs or operational systems (orders, inventory, master data).
  • Background in eCommerce, wholesale, or B2B platform environments.
  • Python for data tooling; Docker, GitHub Actions, AWS.


Your Profile

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
  • 5–8 years of professional experience in software development with a strong product mindset
  • Strong experience with TypeScript and modern React. Backend experience with Node.js, Express or comparable, REST APIs, and PostgreSQL with practical SQL. For mostly building new applications on our modern stack (React 19, Vite, TypeScript, Bun) and occasionally working in an established JavaScript codebase. 
  • Familiarity with modern AI/ML frameworks and agentic AI systems and solid skills in data modelling and building scalable system architectures.
  • Comfort operating in a dynamic, fast-paced environment with shifting priorities.

CaraConsult ist eine spezialisierte Beratungsgesellschaft für die Caravaning-Branche. Unsere Kunden sind vor allem mittelständische Unternehmen rund um Wohnmobile, Wohnwagen und Freizeitfahrzeuge. Wir unterstützen sie dabei, Prozesse zu verbessern, Daten besser zu nutzen, Digitalisierungsvorhaben umzusetzen und wirtschaftlich fundierte Entscheidungen zu treffen.

Unsere IT ist eng mit diesen Themen verbunden. Wir betreiben nicht nur interne Systeme, sondern entwickeln auch eigene Anwendungen, Datenlösungen, Automatisierungen, Schnittstellen und Reportinglösungen. Ein wichtiger Teil unserer Arbeit besteht darin, technische Anforderungen aus dem Alltag zu verstehen und daraus pragmatische, stabile und nutzbare Lösungen zu machen.

Für diese Rolle suchen wir keine Person, die jedes einzelne Thema bereits perfekt beherrscht. Wichtig ist uns ein solides technisches Fundament, Lernbereitschaft, Verantwortungsbewusstsein und die Fähigkeit, sich in gewachsene Systeme und neue Fragestellungen einzuarbeiten.

Aufgaben

  • Du arbeitest an IT- und Digitalisierungsthemen im laufenden Betrieb und in Projekten.   • Du analysierst Anforderungen, ordnest technische Möglichkeiten ein und setzt Verbesserungen pragmatisch um. Dabei geht es nicht nur darum, dass etwas kurzfristig funktioniert, sondern auch darum, dass Lösungen nachvollziehbar, wartbar und langfristig stabil bleiben.
  • Je nach Erfahrung und persönlichem Schwerpunkt kannst du dich stärker in IT-Betrieb, Softwareentwicklung, Datenverarbeitung, Automatisierung, Infrastruktur oder technische Kundenlösungen einbringen. Wichtig ist, dass du technische Themen ganzheitlich betrachten möchtest und verstehst, dass Entwicklung, Betrieb, Dokumentation und kontinuierliche Verbesserung eng zusammenhängen.
  • Du hilfst außerdem dabei, bestehende Lösungen transparenter zu machen, Wissen besser zu dokumentieren und technische Strukturen Schritt für Schritt weiterzuentwickeln.

Qualifikation

Für uns ist es wichtig, dass du ein gutes technisches Gesamtverständnis mitbringst und dich sicher in unterschiedlichen IT-Fragestellungen bewegst.

Besonders relevant sind für uns:

  • mehrjährige Erfahrung im IT-Umfeld, zum Beispiel in Administration, Systembetreuung, technischer Projektarbeit, Digitalisierung, Softwareentwicklung, Datenverarbeitung oder einer vergleichbaren Rolle
  • praktische Erfahrung mit mindestens einer Programmiersprache oder Skriptsprache, zum Beispiel Python, PHP, JavaScript, TypeScript oder einer vergleichbaren Sprache
  • gutes Verständnis für Microsoft 365, insbesondere Benutzer, Gruppen, Berechtigungen, SharePoint, Teams und grundlegende Administrations- oder Supportprozesse

  • Bereitschaft, dich in bestehende Anwendungen, Automatisierungen, Schnittstellen und technische Prozesse einzuarbeiten
  • Grundverständnis für produktive Systeme, Hosting, Deployment, Serverbetrieb oder Cloud-Plattformen
  • Fähigkeit, technische Anforderungen zu analysieren, Prioritäten zu erkennen und pragmatische Lösungen umzusetzen
  • strukturierte Arbeitsweise, Verantwortungsbewusstsein und Bereitschaft, Wissen nachvollziehbar zu dokumentieren
  • Interesse daran, fachliche Anforderungen und Kundenprozesse zu verstehen

Benefits

  • Bei uns arbeitest du in einem modernen Umfeld mit echten Einblicken in Unternehmen, reale Prozesse und konkrete technische Anforderungen. Dich erwartet eine verantwortungsvolle Rolle mit Gestaltungsspielraum, kurzen Entscheidungswegen und direkter Zusammenarbeit.
  • Unser Büro liegt zentral in Bad Homburg, direkt gegenüber vom Kurpark, in einem schönen Altbau mit modernen Arbeitsplätzen und guter Verkehrsanbindung. Wir legen Wert auf ein gutes Miteinander und nutzen gemeinsame Tage im Büro bewusst für Austausch, Teamarbeit und persönliche Abstimmung.
  • Du erhältst flexible Arbeitszeiten, mobiles Arbeiten, eine Ausstattung für dein Homeoffice, regelmäßige Teamevents, gemeinsame Workshops, kostenfreie Getränke im Büro und Möglichkeiten zur fachlichen Weiterentwicklung.
  • Nach der Einarbeitungszeit ist eine überwiegend remote mögliche Tätigkeit realistisch. Gleichzeitig wirst du bei uns nicht allein gelassen: Wir arbeiten dich strukturiert ein, geben dir Einblick in unsere Systeme und unterstützen dich dabei, Schritt für Schritt Verantwortung zu übernehmen.

Diese Rolle passt besonders gut zu Menschen, die technische Breite mögen und nicht nur ein sehr enges Aufgabengebiet bearbeiten möchten. Bei uns gibt es gewachsene Systeme, konkrete Kundenanforderungen und viele Themen, die pragmatisch weiterentwickelt werden müssen. Das erfordert technisches Verständnis, Eigeninitiative und die Bereitschaft, Verantwortung für Lösungen zu übernehmen.

Branchenwissen im Caravaning-Handel brauchst du nicht mitzubringen. Wichtig ist aber, dass du verstehen möchtest, wie unsere Kunden arbeiten und welche technischen Lösungen ihnen im Alltag wirklich helfen.

The role

We are building the AI platform for freight forwarding and expanding our product surface, and we are hiring software engineers across product, AI and platform to do it.

You will build products that do freight forwarding work alongside our customers' teams, operating across the entire shipment lifecycle. You will work across the stack in Python, TypeScript and React, and directly with customers and founders on what gets built.

Everyone here works across the stack, but each engineer has a spike: the area where they set the bar for the team. You spend most of your time where yours is, and lean on your colleagues where theirs are.

🏆 What's the opportunity?

Air freight carries less than 1% of world trade by volume and more than a third of it by value, around $22.7 billion of goods every single day. It's how a vaccine reaches a clinic before it spoils, how a semiconductor arrives before the production line stops, and how a retailer restocks a continent away in three days instead of five weeks. When speed is the whole point, freight flies.

Somebody has to price it, book it and move it, and that work is still done largely by hand, in inboxes and spreadsheets.

For eight years we've been building the data infrastructure underneath it: direct integrations with 75 airlines, the top ten ocean carriers and dozens of GSAs, used every day by 30,000 freight forwarders across 172 countries to hold their rates, price their business and book their freight.

In 2026 we acquired Cargofive, and cargo.one now spans air and ocean, the two modes that carry international trade. That foundation is what makes the next part possible.

In March 2026 we launched the industry's first AI-native operating system for multimodal freight:one workspace where freight teams and AI agents work side by side across rate management, procurement, quoting, booking and support. Crane Worldwide and Yusen Logistics are rolling it out across their global operations.

AI-led engineering is how we build. Engineers write specs and acceptance criteria, agents do much of the implementation, and the engineer owns the architecture, the review and what ships.

We're backed by Index Ventures, Bessemer, Creandum, Point Nine, Next47 and Lufthansa Cargo, which has been an investor in us since 2018.

🚀 What makes this role different

This is an engineering management job for a team where agents do much of the implementation. That changes the job.

When producing code gets cheaper and faster, the bottleneck moves. Throughput depends more on how well engineers define the problem, direct the agents, review what comes back and tell a plausible answer from a correct one.

You'll lead our engineers: what they ship, how good it is, how fast they move, whether the people are growing, and how quickly the team gets better at working AI-led. A lot of what engineering managers know about pacing, estimating, reviewing and measuring a team was calibrated for a different bottleneck. Working out what good looks like now is part of this job.

Today, engineers direct agents on their own work. That's where we are, but it's not the end state. We're building toward fleets of agents that work on their own inside guardrails and harnesses we design, while engineers move up to setting direction, reviewing what comes back, and owning what ships. Part of your job is helping the team get there while keeping the quality bar high.

This is also a player-coach role. You'll stay close enough to the code to keep your judgment sharp and your technical credibility current, while the engineers you lead and what they deliver remain the focus.

🧭 What we're looking for — the part that isn't negotiable

You get more from growing people than from being the smartest person in the room. You've watched someone you managed become better than you at something and enjoyed it. You run real one-to-ones, not status meetings. You give hard feedback early and kindly, and you've done the hard version more than once.

You think in systems. Teams are systems too. You can see why delivery is slipping without needing someone to tell you, and you fix the process rather than working harder inside a broken one.

You're excited about the business. You want to know what your engineers' work is worth and what it does for the customer paying us. You can explain that to them so their work has a point beyond the issue they're closing.

You work at eye level with Product. You co-own what gets built and when, push back on the brief, and don't treat "Product decides, Engineering delivers" as a healthy way to work.

You want to be in the room with customers. Freight forwarders and airlines, directly. You'd rather hear the problem first-hand, and you take your engineers with you.

English is your working language, at close to native fluency. You write and speak it the way you think in it. Almost everything a manager does in a remote-first company is language: the feedback that has to land precisely, the written decision that stops a debate, the difficult conversation where the wrong word costs you trust.

You'll also need:

  • Experience managing engineers: hiring them, growing them, running performance honestly and shipping on a predictable cadence.

  • A backend engineering background, strong architecture instincts and enough technical currency that your engineers respect your technical opinion.

  • A delivery track record. Specific things that shipped, on a schedule you can describe, and an honest account of what slipped and why.

  • Experience building a team, not only running one. You know how to assess for potential, close a candidate and set someone up so their first ninety days work.

  • Genuine engagement with AI-led engineering. You don't need to be an expert, but you can't manage engineers working this way from the outside. You need to use the tools yourself and want to get good at them.

  • Judgment, and the nerve to use it. You'll make calls with incomplete information and own them out loud.

  • Low ego. You take feedback from your own engineers and change your mind in public.

Nice to have: experience with our stack of Python 3, Flask, gRPC, PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery and Kubernetes on GCP; Vue.js; managing a distributed team across several countries; or introducing a new way of working to a team that didn't ask for one.

🎬 A snapshot of what you'll be doing

  • Own delivery. What ships, how good it is and whether the commitments you make hold.

  • Grow the people. One-to-ones that are worth the hour, honest performance conversations, career paths that mean something, and knowing what each person wants next.

  • Hire. You'll own the hiring bar and run your own loops. We hire senior engineers on judgement and character rather than AI experience, and teach them the workflow. You'll be central to making that work.

  • Partner with Product as an equal. Shape the roadmap, negotiate scope and protect engineers from churn that isn't worth it.

  • Raise the team's AI capability. Help engineers use agents better today, spread what works, remove friction, and help evolve our setup toward autonomous agent fleets with the right guardrails and harnesses in place.

  • Stay technical, roughly a day a week. Reviews, a well-chosen piece of work, enough to keep your hands and judgement in.

  • Go to the users. Sit with freight forwarders and airlines, and take your engineers with you.

🤖 What you'd be working with

We're honest about where we are: Everything below is real and running today, but some of it is young, adoption is uneven across our five teams, and the next stage doesn't exist yet. You'd help build it, not inherit it.

How we work AI-led:

  • Work starts from a spec: Tickets and specs are drafted with agent help, against our agreed templates. Once a spec meets the bar, engineers pick it up, refine it, and own the design and architecture decisions; only then do agents start implementing.

  • Conventions for how agents get context, how work runs in parallel, and how the results come back together safely.

  • AI review on every merge request in CI, and a human review standard built for telling a plausible answer from a correct one.

What we've built to make that work:

Our team shared’s mission is deploy AI agents to transform how patients and doctors connect

We believe healthcare shouldn’t be defined by missed calls, endless waiting lines, and overwhelmed staff. Patients and professionals deserve better.

Vocca builds AI voice agents that answer every call instantly, schedule and reschedule appointments, and free up staff to focus on what matters most: care.

Already trusted by 3500+ providers, we’re transforming the patient–provider relationship, one call at a time.

Want to shape the future of healthcare?

Join us !

  • Discover our company culture and values

  • Here is a product Demo

  • Meet the team

  • Article on our seed round of 5,5M$

The problem

Every medical centre has its own rules. Who can book what, with which practitioner, at what time, what to do with an urgent case at 6 pm. Today these rules live in prompts and in the heads of our ops team. Each new clinic takes hours of manual work, and the ops team is the bottleneck of our growth.

We are building the platform that removes that bottleneck. A scenario engine where the behaviour of the agent is structured configuration, not free text. A self-serve onboarding where a clinic connects its software and sets itself up. A dashboard where the medical staff stop executing and start supervising: the agent handles the volume, humans check what matters.

This is the difference between selling a service and selling a product. Every feature you ship here changes how fast Vocca can grow.

What you will do

  • Build features end to end on the platform: backend, dashboard, and the internal tooling that deploys clinics. You own a feature from the spec with the ops team to production.

  • Work on the scenario engine and the self-serve onboarding, the two biggest projects of the team this year.

  • Ship to more than 1,000 medical staff who use the product all day. A small change has an instant impact, which is rare for a team our size.

  • Learn from senior engineers who have built products before, and push them back when you think they are wrong.

Stack

TypeScript everywhere, backend and frontend (Node, monorepo), PostgreSQL, a design system written in code.
We are migrating our last Python services to TypeScript over the coming months.

How we build

  • We use AI seriously. Agents in every workflow, Claude Max provided. A migration estimated at 3 months was done in 2 weeks. If you have built your own agent workflows, you will feel at home. If you want to learn, you will not find a better place.

  • We ship the version that works, then fix the last 1% when it shows up. In healthcare that only works with rigour: tests, small changes, no untested refactoring.

  • We talk every day with the ops team that deploys clinics and the sales team that sells the product. No silos.

Who does well here

  • 2 to 5 years of experience shipping production software, ideally in a startup where you have seen what fast really means.

  • A strong academic background (top engineering school) is a plus. A track record that speaks for itself works just as well.

  • Comfortable in TypeScript and Node. The exact framework matters less than your fundamentals.

  • You know how to scope and cut. Saying no is worth a lot here, because the AI always says yes.

  • You want your work to be used, not just reviewed, and you like seeing the company grow.

Our first engineer arrived with one year of experience. Eighteen months later he was leading a team. We hire on trajectory, and no engineer has left since day one.

What we expect from you

First week

  • Get onboarded on the stack.

  • Ship your first improvement on the dashboard.

First month

  • Own one feature end to end, from the spec with the ops team to production.

First 3 months

  • Ship a piece of the scenario engine or the self-serve onboarding that clinics use in production.

  • Know the product well enough to challenge a spec before building it.

6 to 12 months

  • Own one area of the platform, with the ops team coming to you first.

  • Take part in technical interviews and help the next engineers get onboarded.

Process: 4 steps, fast

  1. 45 min with Nans (Talent).

  2. 45 min with Pierrick, Head of Engineering.

  3. 1h30 in our office with the engineering team, with live coding without AI. We want to see how you think.

  4. 30 min with Hugo, CTO.

Then references and an offer. When the match is obvious, we have made an offer in 24 hours. You get feedback at every step.

Practical

  • Paris, rue d'Alexandrie (Sentier), new offices.

  • 50-70K + BSPCE.

  • Hybrid 3 days at the office.

  • Claude Max provided.

We aim to keep the process within 30 days. You’ll receive continuous feedback throughout.

Why should you join Vocca?

  • An entrepreneurial adventure, with a supportive, high-energy, execution-focused team

  • A product already live, with delighted customers in a fast-growing market (healthcare automation, voice AI)

Über die Position

Gestalte mit uns die digitale Infrastruktur des europäischen Gartenbaus

Connected Growers entwickelt June  - die Plattform, über die Erzeuger, B2B Käufer und Vermarkter effizient zusammenarbeiten. Wir ersetzen fragmentierte Prozesse durch moderne Software und schaffen eine gemeinsame digitale Infrastruktur für eine ganze Branche.

Dafür suchen wir Verstärkung als Tech Lead Marketplace Experience (m/w/d), um nicht nur Software zu entwickeln, sondern ein Team aufzubauen, technische Verantwortung zu übernehmen und gemeinsam mit dem Produkt-Team die Zukunft unserer Plattform zu gestalten.

Deine Rolle bei June

Als Tech Lead Grower Marketplace Experience (m/w/d) verantwortest du die technische Entwicklung unseres Marketplace und der dazugehörigen Services. Du berichtest direkt an unsere CTO Anna.

Du baust einen neuen Engineering Squad von Grund auf auf und übernimmst die technische und fachliche Verantwortung für einen der kommerziell wichtigsten Bereiche von June. Es geht nicht nur darum, gute Software zu bauen: Du setzt technische Richtung, triffst Entscheidungen unter Unsicherheit, entwickelst Menschen, und prägst die Kultur deines Squads. Du sorgst gemeinsam mit dem Produkt-Team dafür, dass wir Funktionen entwickeln, die für unsere Kunden messbaren Mehrwert schaffen.

Wir geben dir den Kontext und den Freiraum, den du brauchst, um deinen Bereich eigenständig zu führen. Im Gegenzug erwarten wir, dass du Verantwortung übernimmst, Entscheidungen triffst und auch für ihre Konsequenzen einstehst – in einem dynamischen Umfeld, in dem sich Prioritäten verändern und Informationen nicht immer vollständig vorliegen.

Du bist kein klassischer People Manager. Du führst über technische Tiefe, Klarheit, Entscheidungen und Vertrauen. Du bleibst hands-on im Code, ohne zum technischen Bottleneck zu werden, triffst Architekturentscheidungen und unterstützt dein Team dabei, gemeinsam hochwertige Software zu entwickeln.

Unser Marketplace basiert auf dem Spryker Commerce OS. Du entwickelst ein klares Verständnis dafür, wann wir innerhalb der Spryker-Konventionen arbeiten, wann wir erweitern und wann eine individuelle Lösung sinnvoll ist. Dabei behältst du immer die langfristige Wartbarkeit und Erweiterbarkeit unserer Plattform im Blick.


Anforderungen

Was du mitbringst

  • Du hast mehrjährige Erfahrung als Tech Lead oder Senior Engineer in Web- und E-Commerce-Anwendungen sowie fundierte praktische Erfahrung mit PHP und Spryker Commerce OS und weißt, wann du innerhalb der Spryker-Konventionen arbeitest, erweiterst oder bewusst davon abweichst.

  • Du bringst Erfahrung mit API- bzw. Spec-first-Entwicklung sowie mit AWS-Cloud-Infrastrukturen, modernen Deployment-Prozessen und Monitoring mit.

  • Du hast bereits Erfahrung im Teamaufbau und weißt, worauf es ankommt.

  • Du hast Verständnis, Interesse und Lust an Produktentwicklung (Software) und Teamentwicklung (Menschen).

  • Du arbeitest eigenverantwortlich, kommunizierst klar, hast hohe Qualitätsansprüche und sprichst fließend Deutsch sowie sehr gutes Englisch.

Das wäre ein Plus

  • Gute Kenntnisse in TypeScript.

  • Erfahrung mit ERP-, Warehouse- oder Commerce-Systemen.

  • Erfahrung mit komplexen Order-, Pricing- oder Inventory/Catalogue-Prozessen.

  • Erfahrung in einem Startup oder schnell wachsenden Technologieunternehmen.


Aufgabenbereich

Was du bei uns bewegst

  • Du verantwortest Architektur, technische Qualität und Weiterentwicklung des Marketplace und seiner Services.

  • Du baust dein Squad auf, entwickelst deine Teammitglieder weiter und schaffst eine Kultur aus Ownership, Pragmatismus und kontinuierlichem Lernen.

  • Du entwickelst eine klare technische Strategie für den Produktbereich Marketplace Experience und triffst bewusste Entscheidungen darüber, wie wir Spryker einsetzen und erweitern.

  • Du arbeitest eng mit dem Produkt-Team zusammen und übersetzt die Bedürfnisse unserer Käufer und Verkäufer in nachhaltige technische Lösungen..

  • Du sorgst dafür, dass dein Team Software kontinuierlich, sicher und zuverlässig ausliefert – von der technischen Spezifikation und Architektur über API-Design und Entwicklung bis hin zu Betrieb, Incident Management und kontinuierlicher Verbesserung.

  • Du übernimmst Verantwortung für Performance, Stabilität, Security und Compliance und stellst sicher, dass technische Risiken früh erkannt, bewertet und bewusst adressiert werden.

  • Du nutzt AI selbstverständlich im Engineering-Alltag und hilfst deinem Team dabei, AI sinnvoll und verantwortungsvoll für Entwicklung, Testing, Dokumentation und Code Reviews einzusetzen.

So arbeiten wir

Unsere Teams verantworten ihren Produktbereich komplett: Architektur, API-Design, Entwicklung, Betrieb, Incidents, Security, Compliance. Die kommerziellen KPIs gehören dazu.

Wir reden mit Kunden, fahren zu ihnen raus, testen unsere Lösungen dort im Betrieb. Verantwortung endet nicht am Merge-Button.


Die Perspektive

Was dich erwartet

  • Du baust etwas auf, statt ein bestehendes Team zu verwalten.

  • Du bekommst einen klar abgegrenzten Verantwortungsbereich und die Freiheit, ihn zu gestalten.

  • Du arbeitest direkt mit CTO und Product Manager und kannst technische, produktbezogene, kulturprägende und kommerzielle Entscheidungen tatsächlich beeinflussen.

  • Du siehst die Konsequenzen deiner Entscheidungen unmittelbar – im Produkt, im Team und im Geschäft.

  • Hybrides Arbeiten in unserem Büro in Köln sowie regelmäßige Besuche bei Kund*innen, Gärtner*innen und Partner*innen vor Ort



Diese Stellenbeschreibung ist bewusst meinungsstark und setzt hohe Standards. Wir suchen nicht den perfekten Lebenslauf, sondern Menschen, die bei Connected Growers glücklich werden. Wenn du nicht alle formalen Kriterien erfüllst, dich aber in der Art, wie wir arbeiten und führen, wiedererkennst, freuen wir uns trotzdem über deine Bewerbung. Was dir an einzelnen Punkten noch fehlt, können wir gemeinsam entwickeln – entscheidend ist, dass du das Mindset und die Bereitschaft mitbringst, in diese Rolle hineinzuwachsen.

Hinweis: Die Stelle wird zunächst über BridgeMaker besetzt und im weiteren Verlauf zu Connected Growers überführt.

📈 Who We Are:

We are rebuilding the energy transaction, making it transparent and fair.

Our goal is to put power back where it belongs, in the hands of customers and to take on one of the most critical problems of our century, access to low cost electricity.

tem exists to fix a broken global energy market that’s long favoured legacy operators, intermediaries, and opaque pricing. Today’s electricity system was not designed for rapid decarbonisation, AI-driven efficiency or fair access for the actual users - businesses and generators.

We’ve built the first AI native transaction infrastructure to reinvent how electricity is bought, sold and priced. Our technology is designed to cut out the inefficient fees, automate complex market flows, and bring transparency and fairness to energy transactions at scale.

In late 2025, after extraordinary growth, we closed a $75 million Series B - led by Lightspeed Venture Partners with participation from Albion, Atomico, Allianz, Hitachi Ventures, Hitachi Ventures, Schroders Capital and others - positioning us for global expansion, deeper product innovation and category leadership.

We’re scaling internationally and building toward a future where AI-driven infrastructure is foundational to electricity markets worldwide.

Since launch, our modern utility product, known as RED, has already facilitated thousands of business customers and billions in energy transaction value, proving that modern software and AI can transform an industry built on legacy systems.

At tem, we’re not just building another energy company, we’re rearchitecting market infrastructure so that transparency, efficiency and sustainability become the default, not the exception.

🏅 The Role:

We're hiring a Staff Software Engineer to join Origination & New Products, a new three-person squad inside Sell Side Growth.

Sell Side Growth originates, contracts, and retains the renewable generators whose volume powers our platform - without generators, there's no product. The engine is scaling fast, and much of the manual process underneath today's pipeline - tendering, contracting, onboarding - needs to be rebuilt to handle that growth rather than buckle under it.

This is a deep, hands-on IC role, not a squad-lead one - that's owned by the Staff/Senior Staff engineer leading the initiative. You're free to go all-in on the hardest technical problems: integration with Rosso (our pricing and settlement engine), Control Room (our core tendering and pipeline platform), and the deal-gating risk tooling that lets us take on genuinely new categories of commercial risk safely. We're not hiring for leadership polish here. We're hiring a ridiculously good engineer.

In your first 12 months, you might:

  • Own architecture-level decisions on the integration-heavy systems connecting Origination & New Products to Rosso, Data, and Billing.

  • Help ship the first new product category live and generating qualified pipeline within 6 months.

  • Help solve the tendering automation problem that currently limits how much volume the team can quote on - one of the highest-leverage levers for supporting our growth.

  • Contribute to productising a currently manual, error-prone pricing process that's already turning away large, complex deals.

  • Design deal-gating risk tooling for commercial risk categories that don't exist yet at tem, within our React/TypeScript and Python/AWS serverless stack.

  • Go deep on hard systems: Own architecture-level decisions on integration-heavy systems, reasoning clearly about boundaries, contracts, and failure modes.

  • Work across boundaries: Deliver on dependencies that sit with teams you have no authority over, such as Rosso, Data, and Billing, getting integrations right without needing to own the relationship.

  • Build with impact: Design, build, and ship the hardest parts of the new-product build sequence yourself, backend-first but comfortable moving into the React/TypeScript front end when it matters.

  • Maintain high standards: Write clean, well-tested code, contribute to code reviews, and help improve team practices and documentation.

🎯 Requirements:

Must-Haves:

  • Deep technical depth in backend and systems design, with a track record of owning architecture-level decisions on complex, integration-heavy systems.

  • Comfortable in our core stack: Python, AWS serverless (Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, EventBridge), and event-driven architectures. React/TypeScript exposure is a plus but not the bar.

  • Comfort operating without a full spec: able to take a defined slice of an ambiguous problem and turn it into a shippable plan.

  • Experience delivering work where a critical dependency sits with a team you have no authority over.

  • Proven product delivery experience: experience as a Full Stack or Backend Engineer in a startup or fast-paced product environment, with ownership of complex projects from start to finish.

Desirable:

  • Prior experience mentoring engineers or setting technical direction, even without a formal leadership title. Not required. We'd rather have a brilliant engineer who has never led a squad than a mediocre one who has.

  • Experience in energy, fintech, or another regulated, high-stakes commercial domain.

  • Exposure to workflow orchestration, event-driven systems, or real-time pricing engines.

  • Experience originating new product lines from scratch rather than only scaling existing ones.

✨ Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive salary - our current band for this role is £104,000 or equivalent in local currency.

    • Up to £1,200 / €1,200 annually to upgrade your remote setup (co-working passes, equipment, etc.).

    • Up to £150 / €150 monthly on anything that supports your wellbeing - from therapy to gym memberships to meditation apps.

🗣️ Interview Process:

Our processes normally take around 2-3 weeks from first call to offer - please let us know about any adjustments to timelines that may be required.

  1. First call with our Talent Team (30 Mins). This is to understand your experience, motivations, and discuss the role in more detail.

About Toptal

Toptal is a global network of top talent in business, design, and technology that enables companies to scale their teams, on-demand. With $200+ million in annual revenue and team members based around the globe, Toptal is the world’s largest fully remote workforce.

We take the best elements of virtual teams and combine them with a support structure that encourages innovation, social interaction, and fun. We see no borders, move at a fast pace, and are never afraid to break the mold.

Position Description:

As SVP, Product, you will shape the vision as to where Toptal’s products and platforms go next and then drive the execution to build them. This is the most senior product role in the company. You will report to the Chief Executive Officer, sit on the executive team, and work collaboratively with our Engineering, Design, Finance, Marketing, New Businesses, Professional Services, and Customer leaders. AI is not a line item on your roadmap. It is the roadmap.

You should be Toptal’s foremost expert on what AI means for products and platforms. That means real depth in fine-tuning and post-training, agent design and evaluation, and the economics of running models in production, along with the judgment to know which applies to us. Work directly with our AI researchers rather than through them. We expect both the AI agenda and the product strategy to originate with you. We will react to your plan rather than hand you ours.

This is a hands-on role. You will write your own specs and pull your own data. When you think an agent could take over a piece of work, you will build a rough version and find out whether it holds up before anyone budgets for it. You will sit in product reviews and say what you actually think. We move fast, and we need Product setting the pace. You will own and set the standards for the hiring bar for the product team, bringing in talent that will advance Toptal to the next level.

Your remit runs across the business: the core platform, the talent and client experiences, the internal systems that run it, the products we take to market, and the data and AI platform underneath them. You will work hand in hand with Engineering on the platform all of it runs on, fold acquisitions and new products into the portfolio, and know growth marketing cold, because how a product reaches the market is part of building it.

Product is yours to shape at blazing speed: scoping, sizing the teams, planning headcount, and defining the role and the bar for every seat. None of that is beneath the role, and we are not interested in someone who thinks these tasks can be done properly by handing them off to HR. Hiring is the highest-leverage work you do, and we want someone who is visibly excited about landing an A player and treats an open seat as urgent. Your own dedication and hard work will set the tone, and the people you bring in should be inspired to do the best work of their careers on this team. We are looking for the person who will define what an AI-native product organization looks like and then run it successfully.

This is a remote position. Resumes and communication must be submitted in English.

Responsibilities:

The following information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or required skills.

AI and agentic product

  • Own Toptal’s AI product strategy: where agents and models belong across the marketplace, the talent and client experiences, our internal systems, and the products we take to market, along with the business outcomes they carry.
  • Decide what we build with AI and what we do not, including build-versus-buy on models and tooling and the packaging and pricing of AI-enabled products.
  • Make AI quality measurable through evals, acceptance bars, and review loops, and partner with Engineering on the platform as its most demanding customer.
  • Rebuild how Product works using AI, raising the output and judgment of every product manager through AI-assisted discovery, research, prototyping, and analysis. Product managers have to want this rather than comply with it, and creating that pull is on you.

Portfolio and operating model

  • Own the vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap for the whole portfolio: what we build, what we sunset, and how investment is distributed across growth, platform, and operational leverage.
  • Establish the product operating model and the metrics behind it, so decisions are made on evidence and user research rather than opinion.
  • Own the product integration of acquisitions and new products, and act as a senior voice of the customer for both talent and clients.

Team and accountability

  • Decide what a product team should look like now that the roles have blurred, where the product manager believes they can design and code, the engineer believes they can do product and design, and the designer believes they can code and do product.
  • Own resourcing and workforce planning, and hit time-sensitive hiring commitments.
  • Review the product work directly, develop people against a clear bar, and raise it as the organization grows.

In the first week, expect to:

  • Work to get up to speed with how the organization runs, including how our operational frameworks work.
  • Begin building relationships with the CEO, the executive team, and your direct reports.
  • Begin learning Toptal’s platform architecture, marketplace dynamics, internal tooling, and current AI initiatives and capabilities.

In the first month, expect to:

  • Assess the current state of the Product organization and its AI maturity: its people, its roadmap, its rituals, and where the gaps are, including the team against the bar this role requires.
  • Bring the executive team a product strategy no one asked you for.
  • Become acquainted with the full product portfolio, the company’s goals, and those you will partner with.
  • Establish a shared view with the CEO and the executive team of the company’s priorities and how product supports them.
  • Start collaborating closely with your product teams.

In the first three months, expect to:

  • Own the product portfolio, its strategy, and its roadmap, and be executing your own plan with at least one AI-enabled capability already in production and measured.
  • Present your resourcing plan and a clear point of view to the executive team on where product investment should concentrate, what should be deprioritized, and why.
  • Establish or refine the product operating model: planning cadence, prioritization framework, and the metrics the organization will be held to, with the trust of the peers and teams you work with most closely.

In the first six months, expect to:

  • Show business impact from AI-enabled products in at least two core surfaces, with the evidence behind it, and visible progress against the top portfolio priorities measured against the metrics you defined.
  • Have the right leadership team in place, with a clear plan to close any remaining gaps.
  • Be inspiring and mentoring the teams you work with, upleveling how the organization brainstorms, collaborates, and executes, and charting a clear path for scaling Product’s impact.

In the first year, expect to:

  • Run a product organization recognized inside and outside Toptal as one of the most advanced in the industry, with AI leverage embedded in the portfolio and the operating model rather than living in a set of pilots.
  • Have built an exceptional product team doing the best work of their careers, with a record of building impactful products in a timely and elegant fashion.
  • Deliver on your roadmap priorities and promises, with a demonstrable link between product investment and business results, and Product established as a trusted, high-leverage function that the rest of the company plans around.

Qualifications and Job Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree is required, preferably in a technical discipline (Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems). Masters is strongly preferred.
  • At least 15 years of proven software Product Management experience.
  • At least 8 years of experience leading Product organizations, including experience leading other product leaders (managing managers).
  • Proven ability to raise the level of a product organization through the people you hire and develop.
  • Proven ownership of resourcing and workforce planning, with a hiring track record you can quantify. You have made the hard calls when someone was not clearing the bar.
  • Experience owning an entire product portfolio at a high-growth technology company, with accountability for business outcomes and not solely delivery.
  • Demonstrated success setting product strategy at the executive level and translating it into an executable roadmap across multiple teams and domains.
  • Experience leading AI-enabled products, with a focus on delivering measurable business outcomes.
  • Deep, hands-on command of modern AI as a product discipline: agentic architectures, harness and orchestration design, retrieval, context engineering, fine-tuning, and evaluation, along with the economics of running models in production. You have shipped these yourself.
  • Further ahead on AI than the executives around you, able to teach it, and proven at moving an organization to adopt something it was not asking for.
  • Growth marketing fluency. You understand acquisition, activation, conversion, and retention well enough to build for them.
  • Experience with marketplace, platform, or two-sided business models is a strong plus.
  • Prior experience working as a Software Engineer is a strong plus.
  • Comfortable working with SQL or spreadsheets to analyze data, as well as conducting research with internal and external users.
  • Ability to creatively craft solutions through data and a user-centric approach.
  • Be meticulous and have a high bar for quality when writing user stories, brainstorming technical approaches, and testing a feature before it is released.
  • Be humble, willing to learn, and do whatever is needed to help us accomplish our goals.
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
